args: set -euo pipefail; t=$(mktemp -d); cargo install -q --path crates/cli --root "$t/bin"; export PATH="$t/bin/bin:$PATH"; awk '/^## Walkthrough/{f=1;next} /^## /{f=0} f' README.md | awk '/^```/{c=!c;next} c' > "$t/walkthrough.sh"; test -s "$t/walkthrough.sh"; cd "$t" && bash -euo pipefail walkthrough.sh; d=$(find "$t" -name decisions.jsonl | head -n 1); test -n "$d"; tail -n 1 "$d" | jq -e '.winner != null'

set -euo pipefail; t=$(mktemp -d); cargo install -q --path crates/cli --root "$t/bin"; out=$("$t/bin/bin/tier-drop" schemas); for n in registry policy task attempt disqualification routing_decision eval_item eval_split eval_run plan; do echo "$out" | grep -q "$n" || { echo "missing schema $n"; exit 1; }; done

evidence_required: ledger verify output naming the tampered line.
objective: Independently verify the CLI, the ledger's tamper detection, dataset filtering by rights and the schemas command.

outputs.purpose: QA verdict for S-03 with the walkthrough and tamper transcripts.

risk_controls: Run in a separate QA context that never implemented the slice; do not edit implementation files; a verdict is accept or reject with the failing check and defect list.
Tampering happens only on a temporary copy of the ledger.
No secret, phone number, account identifier or internal hostname in any file; run gitleaks protect --staged --redact before each commit.
Never write the owner's forbidden organisation name (grep pattern O[K]OA) or the forbidden phrase (grep pattern needs[ ]you); plain, specific prose.
rollback: Delete qa/V-03 and the temporary directories; the implementation branch is unchanged.
steps: Execute the README walkthrough by copying it verbatim into a fresh temporary directory.
Tamper one byte in attempts.jsonl and confirm ledger verify exits 1 naming the line.
Confirm dataset export --purpose train omits an attempt whose rights have train: false.
Confirm tier-drop schemas lists all ten names (registry policy task attempt disqualification routing_decision eval_item eval_split eval_run plan).
